diag.likely_cause: Embedded oxide particles resulting from work roller damage during high-speed hot rolling.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect hot rolling mill work rollers for surface damage and hold the plate for localized surface re-examination.
diag.summary: An isolated vertical dark linear oxide scale mark is present on the lower-right and center regions of the plate, consistent with damaged hot rolling rolls.

diag.likely_cause: Localized yielding of the strip material during uncoiling.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect the uncoiling station equipment, specifically checking strip tension control and leveller entry rolls.
diag.summary: Three small, clustered horizontal crease defects were detected near the bottom of the strip, resulting from localized yielding during uncoiling.

diag.likely_cause: Continuous linear mark produced by coil welding during the strip transition phase.
diag.recommended_action: Check the welder settings and coil transition logs, then verify if the welded seam section requires cropping.
diag.summary: A single horizontal welding line defect of medium scale is centered across the strip.

diag.likely_cause: Oxide scale becoming mechanically embedded into the hot steel surface during rolling operations.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect high-pressure descaling header nozzles for clogs or pressure drops and check entry temperature at the rolling mill.
diag.summary: Multiple small, dark iron scale compressions are scattered across the sheet where unremoved scale was pressed into the steel surface.

diag.likely_cause: Localized corrosion on the steel surface causing deep, fragmented pits.
diag.recommended_action: Hold the coil and inspect upstream pickling, rinsing, and storage areas for chemical contamination or excessive moisture.
diag.summary: Large, highly salient dark pits scattered across the strip indicate severe localized corrosion, requiring coil hold and upstream process verification.

diag.likely_cause: Oxide scale material was not properly removed prior to rolling and was pressed directly into the base metal surface.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect hot rolling descaling spray headers for clogged nozzles or low pressure, and place affected coil on hold for surface inspection.
diag.summary: Multiple small, dark fragments of rolled-in scale are scattered across the surface, indicating primary descaling issues.

diag.likely_cause: Slippage between the finishing mill work rolls and the strip during processing.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect finishing mill work rolls for surface damage and verify roll drive speed synchronization.
diag.summary: A small, isolated horizontal roll printing defect caused by work roll slippage was detected in the center region.

diag.likely_cause: Severe local deformation during processing due to low carbon content in the steel grade.
diag.recommended_action: Verify chemical analysis for low carbon content and inspect rolling mill deformation parameters; hold coil for physical surface inspection.
diag.summary: Multiple fragmented waist folds are scattered horizontally across the surface, consistent with low carbon content deformation.

diag.likely_cause: Accumulation of metallic dust and oil embedded into the iron sheet surface during rolling or handling.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect strip cleaning sections, wringer rolls, and wiper systems along the right side of the processing line to clear oil and dust build-up.
diag.summary: Multiple scattered dark fragmented patches across the right side indicate moderate iron sheet ash contamination from accumulated metallic dust and oil.

diag.likely_cause: Formation of reddish oxide scale caused by high-silicon steel oxidation during the heating process.
diag.recommended_action: Check reheating furnace temperature controls and atmosphere settings for high-silicon steel runs, and inspect descaling effectiveness.
diag.summary: Multiple scattered dark oxide patches are distributed across the sheet, characteristic of high-silicon steel oxidation during heating.

diag.likely_cause: Flaky corrosion and uneven oxidized layers caused by prolonged environmental or moisture exposure.
diag.recommended_action: Check storage environmental/humidity controls and inspect the center surface area prior to downstream processing.
diag.summary: A small, isolated region of secondary rust skin was detected near the center of the steel surface.

diag.likely_cause: Lubricant contamination depositing on the strip surface, forming localized surface oil stains.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect upstream roll seals and lubricant wiping systems for leaks, and hold the coil for surface degreasing.
diag.summary: An extensive isolated dark oil spot was detected across the central region of the strip due to lubricant contamination.

diag.likely_cause: Uneven roll pressure or temperature fluctuations across the mill rolls during rolling.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect rolling mill temperature profiles and roll pressure settings; perform routine surface verification on the affected strip.
diag.summary: Multiple small, low-saliency silk spots are scattered horizontally across the strip due to minor pressure or temperature variations during rolling.

diag.likely_cause: Entrapment of non-metallic slag on the steel surface caused by exposed slag during the hot rolling stage.
diag.recommended_action: Audit hot rolling mill slag skimming and tundish practices; place a quality hold on the coil to assess crop trimming requirements.
diag.summary: A cluster of four large, dark slag inclusions running vertically along the right and center sections indicates slag exposure during hot rolling.

diag.likely_cause: Improper shearing or cutting damage during the strip production process, resulting in a distinct crescent-shaped indentation.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect slitting and trimming shears for blade damage or misalignment; place a hold on the affected coil section for evaluation and potential cropping.
diag.summary: A large, high-saliency crescent gap caused by shearing issues in strip production requires immediate cutter inspection and coil hold.

diag.likely_cause: Uneven or incomplete drying on the strip surface resulting in localized residual moisture marks.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect the drying section air knives and squeegee rollers for uneven pressure or blockages, and verify strip surface condition before coiling.
diag.summary: An extensive, low-contrast water spot spanning diagonally across the strip indicates an uneven drying issue in the processing line.

diag.likely_cause: Friction between the moving steel strip and foreign objects or sharp debris along the processing line.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect line contact points, guides, and wipers for foreign material buildup; place the current coil on hold for surface inspection.
diag.summary: Two large, highly visible bright vertical scratches were detected, likely caused by friction against foreign objects along the production line.

diag.likely_cause: Thermal micro-cracking driven by uneven cooling patterns or excessive residual stress during strip processing.
diag.recommended_action: Hold coil for manual surface inspection and audit cooling section spray nozzles for uniform flow and pressure.
diag.summary: Multiple scattered crazing defects with high saliency observed across all strip zones indicate widespread surface micro-cracking from uneven cooling.

diag.likely_cause: Excessive processing temperature or uneven cooling across the strip, leading to scattered and loose scale formation.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect cooling zone temperature controls and spray nozzle uniformity; verify descaling system pressure before proceeding.
diag.summary: Scattered fragmented oxide scale has formed across multiple surface regions due to temperature control or uneven cooling issues.

diag.likely_cause: Entrapment of non-metallic smelting residue or slag embedded into the steel substrate during rolling.
diag.recommended_action: Inspect upstream steelmaking degassing/slag-separation processes and perform standard surface verification on the affected coil length.
diag.summary: An isolated, small vertical linear inclusion caused by smelting residue was detected along the center of the strip.

diag.likely_cause: Localized surface indentation resulting from mechanical damage or debris on the work rolls or tension rollers.
diag.recommended_action: Log defect location and inspect work rolls and tension rollers during the next scheduled maintenance; release current coil.
diag.summary: A single tiny, low-saliency rolled pit was detected in the center of the sheet, requiring standard roll surface monitoring.
